newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire calls 15-year-olds to join war.
newsitem.headline: Zaire calls 15-year-olds to join war.

text.p: Zaire on Monday called on its youth from the age of 15 to join special brigades to combat rebels who have overwhelmed its mercenary-backed army.

"The Ministry of National Defence informs all young people between the age of 15 and 18, with at least four years of post-primary education, keen on a career in the army to enrole at the nearest gendarmerie post to their residence," a statement by Defence Minister General Likulia Bolongo Lingbangi said.

The statement said the recruitment was to increase the efficiency of the army "in the face of aggression from neighbouring countries". Defence officials said the government's target was to raise up to 26,000 new troops.

"Parallel to the acquisition of high performance materials, the programme to put in place these rapid intervention brigades aims at increasing the power of the Zairean army in order that it should become a genuine army of dissuasion, and an effective ring of defence at the heart of Africa," the statement said.
It added that military trials of Rwandan and Ugandan troops the government says were captured during fighting in eastern Zaire were due to begin on Tuesday in Kinshasa.
A senior defence ministry official said earlier Zaire expected troops from Morocco, Togo and Chad to help its army contain a rebel campaign that has spread to the mineral-producing Shaba Province.
